title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a working page from the notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. It sets up the formal framework (Kan extension plus Dold–Kan) in which a 'de Rham-type' cochain theory on simplicial sets is determined by a cosimplicial object.

(1) Top block. Hom^!_L denotes colimit-preserving (left-adjoint type) functors, presumably subject to a linearity condition L. The block records two equivalences:
- a colimit-preserving functor (Ss)° → B (B additive) is the same as one B_0 → B;
- a colimit-preserving functor (Ss) → A (A additive) is the same as one A_0 → A.
Here A_0 is the free additive cocompletion of simplicial sets, namely simplicial abelian groups Ab_Δ ≃ Ab_* ≃ chain complexes Ab. (Dold–Kan). Dually B_0 = A_0° ≃ (Ab_*)° ≃ (Ab^*)°, with G_0 = (F_0)°.
The universal functors are (Ss) → A_0, X ↦ Z[X] = C_*(X), and its opposite F_0: (Ss)° → B_0. He notes F_0 ∈ Ab^*_*, i.e. it is given by a cosimplicial/simplicial bigraded object.

(2) Ω block. Ω_L ≃ B_0 → Ab_*° ≃ Ab.°, and Ω'_L ≃ A_0 → Ab_* ≃ Ab., with the arrows labelled 'pl. fid.' (pleinement fidèle, fully faithful). He also writes Hom(Δ°, Ab_*°) ≃ (Ab^*_*)°.

(3) Boxed formula. The data are Ω (a cosimplicial complex, e.g. de Rham / divided-power forms on the standard simplices), F, L_* and L.. In the case A = Ab, the induced functor is
F(X_*) = Ω_*(C_*(X)) = Ω.(C.(X)).
So the cochain theory attached to Ω is the Kan extension of Ω along Δ → Ss. It factors through the chain complex of X: an 'end/tensor' of Ω with Z[X].

(4) Representability chain. For a simplicial abelian group L_*:
Hom_Δ̂(X_*, L_*) ≃ Hom(C_*(X), L_*) ≃ Hom(C.(X), L.) ≃ Hom^*(L^*_*, C^*(X)) ≃ Hom^·(L^·, C^·(X)).
This is the free–forgetful adjunction, then Dold–Kan normalization, then passage to dual cochain complexes. It expresses morphisms into a simplicial abelian group L (an Eilenberg–MacLane-type object) in terms of cochains on X.

(5) Rotated part: the nerve–realization adjunction for A ⊂ Â.
- Colimit-preserving φ: Δ̂_s → A correspond to Φ: Δ̂_s × A° → Ab (and to cosimplicial objects Δ → A).
- Hom(φ(X), M) = Φ(X, M) is representable in M.
- This gives a right adjoint Ψ with Hom(φ(X), M) ≃ Hom_Δ̂s(X, Ψ(M)) and Ψ(M)_n = Hom(φ(Δ^n), M).
- He also considers restriction along semi-simplicial sets: Hom_!(Δ̂_s, A) → Hom_!(Δ̂, A).

Purpose: to characterize cochain functors such as the PD de Rham complex on simplicial sets as Kan extensions of cosimplicial complexes, and to compare them with singular cochains via representing objects.
errors: Hom(C.(X),L.) ≃ Hom^·(L^·, C^·(X)) needs finiteness or duality hypotheses: L degreewise free of finite type, or the dual taken in a suitable sense. As written it is only formal.
The subscript under the third Hom looks like 'Ens' in the transcription. Mathematically it should be Hom of chain complexes (or of graded abelian groups), not of sets.
The notation mixes C_*(X_*) and C_*(X), and Ω_* with Ω.; this is harmless but inconsistent.

ideas.what: Colimit-preserving functors from simplicial sets to a cocomplete category ≃ cosimplicial objects; realization φ with right adjoint Ψ(M)_n = Hom(φ(Δ^n), M)
ideas.modern_name: nerve–realization adjunction / left Kan extension along Yoneda
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) uses this systematically; SGA4 exposé I for the general Kan extension along Yoneda

ideas.what: Additive version: linear colimit-preserving functors factor through simplicial abelian groups ≃ chain complexes
Cochain functor F(X) = Ω.(C.(X)) attached to a cosimplicial complex Ω (de Rham/PD forms on simplices)
ideas.modern_name: simplicial de Rham / Sullivan–Cartan cochain models via cosimplicial forms; Thom–Whitney / polynomial forms

ideas.what: Representability: Hom(X, L) ≃ Hom(C(X), L) ≃ Hom(L^dual, C^*(X))

deep.surprise_reason: Standard formal machinery: Kan extension, nerve–realization and Dold–Kan, set up for the PD de Rham cochain comparison. The interest is only that it is a preliminary scaffolding for the integral divided-power de Rham model of cochains. Nothing on this page goes beyond known material.
transcription_corrections: 'plfid' / 'cplfid' should read 'pl. fid.' (pleinement fidèle = fully faithful) on the arrows B_0 → Ab_*° and A_0 → Ab_*.
'B_0 ≃ (Ab_*)°' with a second line '≃ (Ab*)°' (chain vs cochain notation).
Under 'A_0 = B_0°' there is an inserted '≃ Ab_*'; it is not struck through.
The bracket label '[-Hom-]' at the left is a crossed-out 'Hom' with '𝓛' above; similarly '[-Ω_L-]' is a crossed-out label.
'C_{*∈}' at left is likely 'C_*' with a stray mark; 'C^{*Q}' is likely 'C^*' with marks.
